note: The questions of the preliminary (no laboratory) screening: the 28 Stage 1 predictors of the project, with the value ranges seen in the training data (CKD_400k.csv; the earlier CKD_Risk_Progression_Dataset_2026.csv has the same ones). Nothing is asked that the model does not use. The model file is checked against this list (names, answers and ranges) before screening is switched on, and the training notebook reads this same file; see ml/README.md. Three diet questions (SugaryDrinksAddedSugar, UltraProcessedFoodFrequency, SaturatedFatDairyIntake) were added after a column-by-column audit of CKD_400k.csv found a plausible, consistent direction for each; see ml/DATASET_AUDIT_CKD_400k.md. Blank answers in the training data for SugaryDrinksAddedSugar (10.7%) were recoded to 'None' and blank answers for UltraProcessedFoodFrequency (2.3%) were recoded to 'Never' (an assumption, the same kind already made for Alcohol_Consumption); SaturatedFatDairyIntake had no blanks.

steps.title: About you
steps.intro: A few basic facts. Kidney risk is estimated for adults.

steps.title: Health history
steps.intro: Conditions a doctor has told you about. Answer from what you know; you can leave the rest as No.

steps.title: Medicines
steps.intro: Medicines you take now. Some are used for the heart or blood pressure, and some can affect the kidneys.

steps.title: Lifestyle
steps.intro: Everyday habits. Choose the answer that fits most weeks.

questions.name: Country
questions.label: Where do you live?
questions.hint: If your country is not listed, choose Other.
questions.why: The model was built with data from several countries.

questions.name: Sex
questions.label: Sex assigned at birth
questions.hint: Asked only when your gender answer does not already tell us.
questions.why: The model was trained on sex assigned at birth, and some kidney test results are worked out differently for the two. Your gender answer is still saved exactly as you chose it.

asked_through.label: Gender
asked_through.hint: Choose the one that describes you best. It is saved as you chose it.
asked_through.why: Nephron shows, without names, how kidney risk compares between genders among people who use it. For the risk estimate itself, an answer like Gay man is read as male and Lesbian woman as female; for the others we ask one extra question.

questions.name: Ethnicity
questions.label: Ethnic background
questions.hint: Choose the closest group.
questions.why: Risk differs between groups in the data the model learned from.

questions.name: Age
questions.label: Age
questions.why: The chance of kidney disease rises with age.
questions.range_note: Enter your age in whole years.

questions.name: BMI
questions.label: Height and weight
questions.why: Body mass index is worked out from your height and weight.
questions.range_note: Your height and weight give a body mass index (BMI).

questions.name: Obesity
questions.label: Obesity
questions.why: Worked out from your BMI (30 or more). You are not asked this separately.

questions.name: Diabetes
questions.label: Has a doctor told you that you have diabetes?
questions.hint: Type 1, type 2 or diabetes found in pregnancy that has stayed.
questions.why: Long-term high blood sugar can damage the kidneys' filters.

questions.name: Hypertension
questions.label: Has a doctor told you that you have high blood pressure?
questions.hint: Also called hypertension.
questions.why: High blood pressure can damage the small blood vessels of the kidneys.

questions.name: Cardiovascular_Disease
questions.label: Do you have heart or blood-vessel disease?
questions.hint: For example a heart attack, angina or a stroke.
questions.why: The heart and kidneys share many of the same risk factors.

questions.name: Heart_Failure
questions.label: Has a doctor told you that you have heart failure?
questions.why: A weak heart can reduce blood flow to the kidneys.

questions.name: Hyperlipidemia
questions.label: Do you have high cholesterol or other high blood fats?
questions.hint: Also called hyperlipidemia.
questions.why: Blood fats are linked to blood-vessel disease, including in the kidneys.

questions.name: Kidney_Stones
questions.label: Have you ever had kidney stones?
questions.why: Stones can affect how well the kidneys work over time.

questions.name: Recurrent_UTI
questions.label: Do you often get urinary tract infections (UTIs)?
questions.hint: Several in a year.
questions.why: Repeated infections can affect the kidneys.

questions.name: Autoimmune_Disease
questions.label: Do you have an autoimmune disease?
questions.hint: For example lupus or rheumatoid arthritis.
questions.why: Some autoimmune diseases can involve the kidneys.

questions.name: Family_History_CKD
questions.label: Does a close relative have chronic kidney disease?
questions.hint: A parent, brother or sister.
questions.why: Kidney disease can run in families.

questions.name: ACE_Inhibitor
questions.label: Do you take an ACE inhibitor?
questions.hint: A blood pressure or heart medicine, for example lisinopril or enalapril.
questions.why: Some medicines for blood pressure and the heart change how the kidneys work.

questions.name: ARB
questions.label: Do you take an angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB)?
questions.hint: A blood pressure or heart medicine, for example losartan or valsartan.
questions.why: Some medicines for blood pressure and the heart change how the kidneys work.

questions.name: Diabetes_Medication
questions.label: Do you take medicine for diabetes?
questions.hint: For example metformin or insulin.
questions.why: This shows how diabetes is being treated.

questions.name: Diuretic
questions.label: Do you take a diuretic (water pill)?
questions.hint: For example furosemide or hydrochlorothiazide.
questions.why: Diuretics change how much fluid the kidneys have to handle.

questions.name: Statin
questions.label: Do you take a statin?
questions.hint: A cholesterol medicine, for example atorvastatin or simvastatin.
questions.why: Statins are used for blood fats and heart protection.

questions.name: NSAID_Usage
questions.label: Do you use NSAID pain relievers?
questions.hint: Anti-inflammatory pain relievers such as ibuprofen or naproxen.
questions.why: Frequent use of some pain relievers can strain the kidneys.

questions.name: Smoking_Status
questions.label: Do you smoke?
questions.why: Smoking harms blood vessels, including those of the kidneys.

questions.name: Alcohol_Consumption
questions.label: How much alcohol do you drink?
questions.hint: Moderate is about one or two drinks a day at most. Heavy is more than that.
questions.why: Heavy drinking is linked to blood pressure and kidney harm.

questions.name: Exercise_Hours_Per_Week
questions.label: Hours of exercise in a usual week
questions.why: How much you exercise, in hours. Your activity level (sedentary, light, moderate or active) is worked out from it, so you are not asked twice.
questions.range_note: Enter hours per week (0 if none).

questions.name: Physical_Activity_Level
questions.label: How active are you?
questions.why: Regular activity helps blood pressure and blood sugar.

derived_from.note: Worked out from your exercise hours.
derived_from.source: Cut-offs read from the training data (CKD_400k.csv): they agree with the dataset's own activity level in 97.9% of its 400,000 rows.

questions.name: Water_Intake_L
questions.label: Water you drink in a day
questions.hint: About 4 glasses is 1 litre.
questions.why: How much you drink each day.

questions.name: Fast_Food_Frequency_Per_Week
questions.label: Fast-food meals in a usual week
questions.why: Fast food is often high in salt.
questions.range_note: Enter how many times per week (0 if never).

questions.name: SugaryDrinksAddedSugar
questions.label: How much sugar-sweetened drink do you have?
questions.hint: Soda, sweetened juice drinks, sweetened tea or coffee, energy drinks - not the sugar you add yourself.
questions.why: Regularly sweetened drinks are linked with a higher rate of CKD in this dataset.

questions.name: UltraProcessedFoodFrequency
questions.label: How often do you eat packaged or ultra-processed food?
questions.hint: Instant noodles, packaged snacks, sausages and other processed meat, ready-made meals.
questions.why: A higher frequency is linked with a higher rate of CKD in this dataset.

questions.name: SaturatedFatDairyIntake
questions.label: How much saturated fat and full-fat dairy do you eat?
questions.hint: Fatty meat, butter, cheese, full-cream milk and similar foods.
questions.why: A higher intake is linked with a higher rate of CKD in this dataset.

questions.name: Sleep_Duration_Hours
questions.label: Hours of sleep on a usual night
questions.why: Poor sleep is linked to blood pressure.
questions.range_note: Enter hours of sleep on a usual night.

range_policy: min/max are the ranges the model was TRAINED on; valid_min/valid_max are the realistic limits an answer is accepted within. An answer outside the training range is accepted and flagged on the result. An option's model_value (e.g. Philippines -> Other) is what the model receives; the person's own answer is what is saved.
